Universal and Existential Quantifiers

A game on the number line teaches the quantifiers. Swap the order and watch the same game collapse.

One side moves first and the other side answers. 'For all' demands an answer to every challenge. 'There exists' needs just one good answer. Swapping the order changes the claim itself. This pattern becomes the epsilon-delta definition later.

For example, for every 🧑 classmate, someone taller exists. But one person taller than everybody does not exist. A single swap changes the whole meaning.

∀x ∃y (y>x)\forall x \,\exists y \,(y > x)∀x∃y(y>x)
¬(∀x ∃y)=∃x ∀y\lnot(\forall x \,\exists y) = \exists x \,\forall y¬(∀x∃y)=∃x∀y

The negation flips every quantifier (∀\forall∀ becomes ∃\exists∃, ∃\exists∃ becomes ∀\forall∀) and rewrites the final implication via ¬(P→Q)≡P∧¬Q\lnot(P \to Q) \equiv P \land \lnot Q¬(P→Q)≡P∧¬Q. The first option fails to flip the δ\deltaδ quantifier, the third keeps the implication instead of turning it into a conjunction, and the fourth never flips the outer ∀ε\forall\varepsilon∀ε and merely reverses the inequalities.

  2. Disprove the second statement. Whatever candidate y0∈Ry_0 \in \mathbb{R}y0​∈R is proposed, set x=y0+1x = y_0 + 1x=y0​+1; then x∈Rx \in \mathbb{R}x∈R and y0>xy_0 > xy0​>x is equivalent to y0>y0+1y_0 > y_0 + 1y0​>y0​+1, i.e. 0>10 > 10>1, which is false.

    Hence no y0y_0y0​ satisfies "y0>xy_0 > xy0​>x for all xxx" — ∃y ∀x (y>x)\exists y\ \forall x\ (y > x)∃y ∀x (y>x) is false. In the scene the candidate y=2y = 2y=2 falls to x′=3x' = 3x′=3.
